gallery.title: ZIP Map, Network & Nested Stacked Bars
gallery.description: A geographic Scatterplot positions ten nodes using ZIP geometry. Graph links connect those same positions above ZIP polygons colored by total sightings. Each node connects to a message frame containing twelve monthly bars stacked by five travel modes.

file.name: case2.csv + geo graph + NYC ZIP geometry
file.description: case2.csv contains sighting observations keyed by incident_zip. The geo dataset pairs 120 monthly observations for ten nodes with thirteen source–target edges. Both maps join the same case-owned NYC ZIP GeoJSON; 177 geometry features match ZIPs in case2.csv; unmatched ZIP values are omitted.

gallery.composition: Start with the independently bound Polygon, geographic Scatterplot, and Stacked Bar. First position nodes by joining geo.point to the ZIP geometry. Drag Graph Link (Geographic) directly onto the Scatterplot to add links at those node positions. Layer the Scatterplot over the Polygon, then nest the Stacked Bar into the Scatterplot points. Each nested chart inherits its node’s point filter and shows that node’s twelve monthly observations. Enable its message frame and offset it from the point: the arrow stays anchored to the original node. Polygon color sums sighting_count for each matched ZIP geometry.

editorHelp.introduction: The Polygon map, geographic Scatterplot, and Stacked Bar are prepared on the canvas. Add Graph Link from the chart catalog first.

steps.title: Add the network links
steps.source: Graph Link (Geographic) in the top Chart Blocks catalog
steps.action: Choose Geographic in the Coordinate filter and open Geographic line in the top Chart Blocks catalog. Drag the Graph Link (Geographic) tile directly onto the Scatterplot map, then release inside the map.
steps.result: Links connect the ten existing Scatterplot nodes using the prepared graph data.

steps.title: Layer the maps
steps.source: Geographic Scatterplot map on the canvas
steps.action: Drag the Scatterplot map onto the interior of the Polygon map. Release when the destination highlights with Layer.
steps.result: ZIP polygons, Scatterplot nodes, and network links share the same map.

steps.title: Nest bars at the map nodes
steps.target: Layered map center → a Scatterplot node
steps.action: Hold the Stacked Bar and drag through the map’s central Enter circle. Keep holding, move onto a visible Scatterplot node, and release when Nested highlights that point.
steps.result: Each node gets a Stacked Bar showing its twelve months and five travel modes, filtered by point.

steps.title: Move the profiles away from the map
steps.source: A nested Stacked Bar’s frame settings
steps.target: An offset beside its original map node
steps.action: Open the nested chart’s configuration, enable Connect frame to parent, and adjust Offset X and Offset Y to move its frame clear of neighboring charts. Repeat for overlapping profiles.
steps.result: Each offset profile keeps a connecting tail anchored to its original map node.
